security_spec.violation_condition: OpenSBI writes menvcfg.CBZE, menvcfg.CBCFE, or menvcfg.CBIE and returns to S-mode via MRET without an ordering barrier (fence or sfence.vma) between the CSR write and MRET, allowing S-mode CBO instructions to execute before the menvcfg write is architecturally visible. Additionally, OpenSBI's HSM suspend/resume path fails to save and restore menvcfg, causing S-mode to observe stale CBO enable/disable state after resume. Additionally, OpenSBI writes to the WARL menvcfg.CBIE field and assumes the written encoding took effect without reading back to confirm the hardware-granted value, resulting in a mismatch between the firmware-expected CBO.INVAL behavior (flush vs invalidate) and the actual hardware behavior granted to lower privilege modes.
security_spec.summary: OpenSBI must fence after menvcfg CMO field writes before MRET, save/restore menvcfg across HSM suspend/resume, and read back WARL menvcfg.CBIE after write — otherwise S-mode can execute cache operations M-mode intended to block, or execute invalidate when M-mode expected flush
